obtained.how: Internet Archive item developmentoffis0002unse (Volume II of the atlas, NOAA Northwest Fisheries Center library copy; openly downloadable, not a lending item). Volume III (the white perch account) and Volume I (chain pickerel, Jones, Martin & Hardy) exist on Internet Archive only as lending-restricted items, not opened

bibliography.checked_against: Volume II's title page (PDF p. 7) and general introduction (printed p. 1); Volume III from the reference list of Fischer, Hall & Sullivan 1989b
bibliography.corrections: The ledger's 'Hardy. 1978' is incomplete and covers two different volumes. (1) Banded killifish (Table 3.6-1): Hardy, J. D., Jr. 1978. Development of fishes of the Mid-Atlantic Bight: an atlas of egg, larval and juvenile stages. Volume II, Anguillidae through Syngnathidae. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Biological Services Program, FWS/OBS-78/12 (January 1978), Chesapeake Biological Laboratory, University of Maryland. (2) White perch (Table 3.5-2, §3.6.1): the same series, Volume III, Aphredoderidae through Rachycentridae, FWS/OBS-78/12, 1978 (as cited by Fischer, Hall & Sullivan 1989b; title page not seen). Split into Hardy 1978a and 1978b. (3) The chain pickerel row's 'Jones, Martin & Hardy 1978' is yet another work, Volume I (Acipenseridae through Ictaluridae), and needs its own ledger entry.
bibliography.note: The series is in six volumes (Vol. II, printed p. 1): I Acipenseridae–Ictaluridae, II Anguillidae–Syngnathidae, III Aphredoderidae–Rachycentridae, IV Carangidae–Ephippidae, V Chaetodontidae–Ophidiidae, VI Stromateidae–Ogcocephalidae.

claims.claim: banded killifish hatch at 5.3–6.4 mm TL (Hardy 1978, via Shute et al. 1983)
claims.location: Vol. II p. 159 (PDF p. 171), Fundulus diaphanus account, Yolk-sac larvae
claims.conditions: literature compilation (two cited sources); the length type is not stated for the hatching length, but the account's figures and proportions are in TL (yolk-sac larvae 5.6 and 5.8 mm TL; 'proportions expressed as times in TL at 7.1 mm')
claims.note: Hardy's 7.1 mm is the MAXIMUM yolk-sac-larva length, on a TL basis. The same table's '7.1 mm SL' (credited to 'repo') may be a misreading of this; check its source. The same account gives incubation of 11–12 days at 22.0–26.5 °C and 16–18 days at 12–14 °C, and spawning at 22–32.2 °C.

claims.claim: white perch mature at 72–80 mm (males) and 90–98 mm (females), ages 2–4 (Hardy 1978, Mansueti 1964, via Stanley & Danie 1983)
claims.note: In Volume III, which is not openly available (Internet Archive lending item developmentoffis0003jerr; HathiTrust refused with a bot check).

claims.claim: sudden drops of 2–3 °C kill white perch eggs and drops of 4–5 °C are lethal (AuClair 1960 and Hardy 1978, via Fischer, Hall & Sullivan 1989b)
claims.note: Volume III not obtained. The intermediary is checked in Fischer_etal_1989b.json: Fischer et al. do say it, crediting AuClair 1960 and Hardy 1978 jointly.

claims.claim: chain pickerel incubation 11 d at 10.0 °C, 5 d at 14.4 °C, 2.5 d at 17.2 °C (Jones, Martin & Hardy 1978, via FishBase)
claims.note: A different work (Volume I, Jones, Martin & Hardy), matched to this key only by the words 'Hardy 1978'. Not openly available (Internet Archive lending item developmentoffis0001unse).

tried.note: Volume III (Hardy 1978, white perch): access-restricted lending item ('inlibrary'); not opened. Library route: U.S. Fish Wildl. Serv. FWS/OBS-78/12, Vol. III
Volume I (Jones, Martin & Hardy 1978, chain pickerel): access-restricted lending item; not opened
Cloudflare bot check; not worked around (HathiTrust may hold full-view copies of these federal documents for the human to open)

notes: The paper cites Hardy only through intermediaries (Stanley & Danie 1983; Fischer, Hall & Sullivan 1989b; Shute, Lindquist & Shute 1983; FishBase). Only the killifish value could be read in the original. Volume II also has the other Fundulus species (its killifish key starts on printed p. 139), if needed.
